reasoning: The package is a standard AUR binary package that downloads prebuilt archives from the official GitHub releases (https://github.com/liixini/skwd-wall/releases) with pinned SHA256 checksums. The PKGBUILD contains only static variable assignments at the top level with no command substitution or dynamic evaluation. The skwd-deck.install script performs routine systemd user service cleanup during package removal using standard patterns (iterating /run/user directories, using runuser for systemctl --user). No code injection, no execution of fetched content, no contact with unrelated hosts, and no obfuscated commands are present.
disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by tool failure, not substantive security concerns. The qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 model encountered HTTP 400 BadRequestError when attempting to audit PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO, leaving 2 of 3 files unreviewed and forcing an inconclusive verdict. The deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash model successfully reviewed all three files and found them safe. The openrouter/free report is marked advisory:true and does not count as a vote, though it corroborates the safe finding.
coverage_issues: qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507 failed to audit PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO due to HTTP 400 errors, leaving the most critical files (build script and metadata) unreviewed
learnings: When a model encounters API errors (HTTP 400/500) during file review, the audit tool should automatically retry the failed requests before marking the overall result as inconclusive
The audit tool should distinguish between 'model could not complete review due to tool error' and 'model reviewed files and found them inconclusive' - these require different handling

For packages with tool failures on critical files (PKGBUILD, .install), the system should prioritize re-running with a different model rather than publishing an inconclusive verdict that triggers unnecessary escalation
